Q: Areal features are elements shared by various languages in a region, even those not from the same language family, and particularly when they don't originate from any of the ancestors of any of the language families. An example of an areal feature are X words. In linguistics, an X word is a form of reduplication as a widespread areal feature in the languages of South Asia, and is a linguistic feature found all across the Indian sprachbund. In the Indian subcontinent, the Indo-European languages, Dravidian languages, Austroasiatic languages, and Sino-Tibetan languages, all have this feature, even though this feature didn't exist in the ancestor of any of these languages families.
